$doc: Stat's appearance, as data — the source of the `@component stat` block in css/components.css. Same contract as components/button/definition.json: a plain string is a structural literal, {"token": "x"} binds --x, and an array is a sequence of both. Stat is the third shape the pilot needed: no variants, no sizes, no states, no parts — one selector and one rule. It is the case that proved a definition may declare nothing but its base (the sections it left out were OPTIONAL rather than empty; since the rules became one list, `rules` holding a single entry says the same thing with nothing to leave out), and it is also the one where a token binds a whole compound value (`border` is `--rule-strong`, a width, a style and a colour in one token, which is why the light-to-dark judgement about that rule lives in tokens.json and not here).

block.title: Stat
note: Shares `--text-display` with `.fact__num` and `.t-display--lg`. It used to
carry its own clamp, one 0.5vw step away from the fact number's — the same
size twice, drifted apart by nobody's decision.
